summary: Both editions were independently reviewed against all five paragraphs of the selected Greek. Neither presents a concrete fidelity defect: both preserve the dialogue, whole-heart repentance and turning, remaining-life righteousness, service according to the Lord’s will, healing, emphatic prohibitions, divine ability to save and destroy, and the heart-purification conditions. Repentance and service terminology accord with current policy. The notes accurately distinguish the working Greek from the reported Latin alternatives and retain the mandate boundary without importing the Latin amen. Acceptance is limited to the supplied working source and attributed evidence; it does not authenticate unseen images or certify exhaustive collation. Any proposed replacement would require fresh review.
